analysis.analysis: The composition layer serves a complete biography of the authorial mantle in answer to a direct identity query: American poet, independent scholar, Detroit-area World Literature teacher, PhD, working in operative semiotics and SPXI inscription analysis on how signs survive compression — with all three distributed-journal instruments (Provenance: Journal of Forensic Semiotics, Machine-Mediated Reception Studies, Grammata: Journal of Operative Philology) cited as venues contributed to. Three findings and a comedy. First, mantle consolidation: the author-function has a machine-served biographical identity anchored to the academia.edu profile. Second, the fold holds: no civil identity appears anywhere in the composition — the mantle functions as the person. Third, journal-title adoption: the journal apparatus reads to the machine as a publication record. The comedy is a genre misfiling with characterological output: the surface devotes a titled section, a Notable Traits bullet, and its closing assessment to 'amateur dinosaur enthusiast' — a trait derived from the archive's semiotic scholarship analyzing a dinosaur portrait in banknote-engraving conventions (the raptor posed as Jackson on the $20). Analysis of a dinosaur image became enthusiasm for dinosaurs. The phrase 'mental skyscrapers of dinosaur names' originates in 'Contributor Bio,' an absurdist poem in the collection Pearl and Other Poems (Alexanarch deposit #329, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18293949; MANUS provenance identification, 2026-07-11) — the surface ingested a parody of the contributor-bio genre as the genre it parodies: the poem performed a fake bio, and the machine believed the performance because the title announced it. The trait is therefore not confabulation but genre-blind faithful extraction, from two sources of misread genre at once: intaglio scholarship read as hobby, absurdist self-portraiture read as fact. Related: heteronymic-provenance-theory (the heteronym-structure line). Full transcript at captures/lee-sharks-bing-copilot-biography-20260711.md. Second run and screenshots pending.

notes._paired_note: Four observations on one address across three months. The 2026-08-12 pair is the load-bearing one: ChatGPT and Perplexity issued THIS EXACT STRING on the same day, both unprimed and signed out. ChatGPT resolved first-pass and disambiguated the shark; Perplexity found nothing notable and then reconstructed the archive after one corrective prompt. Availability is not priority.
